topic: Andhra Movement & Formation of Andhra Pradesh

items.title: Roots of the Andhra Movement (1913–1950)
items.body:
## The demand for a separate Andhra

- Telugu-speaking districts lay in the **Madras Presidency**, where the Telugu elite felt overshadowed by Tamil dominance in jobs, education and politics.
- The **first Andhra Mahasabha** met in **1913 at Bapatla**, formally demanding a **separate Andhra province**. A separate Andhra unit within the Congress followed in **1917**.

## Sri Bagh Pact (1937)

- Within the Andhra region, the backward **Rayalaseema** feared domination by the more developed **Coastal Andhra**.
- The **Sri Bagh Pact (1937)** — signed at *Sri Bagh*, the Madras home of **Kasinadhuni Nageswara Rao** — assured Rayalaseema of safeguards on **irrigation, education and the location of the capital/High Court**.

## The linguistic-states debate

- After independence, the **Dhar Commission (1948)** and the **JVP Committee (1949)** (Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya) advised **against** immediate linguistic reorganisation, fearing threats to national unity.
keyPoints: First Andhra Mahasabha held in 1913 at Bapatla, demanding a separate Andhra province in Madras Presidency.
Sri Bagh Pact (1937) reassured Rayalaseema against Coastal Andhra dominance, promising safeguards.
Sri Bagh Pact signed at the Madras residence of Kasinadhuni Nageswara Rao.
Dhar Commission (1948) and JVP Committee (1949) opposed immediate linguistic reorganisation of states.
items.mnemonic: Two pacts, two regions: Sri Bagh (1937) = Coastal + Rayalaseema; Gentlemen's (1956) = Andhra + Telangana.
items.source: Standard accounts of the Andhra movement; Wikipedia — Sri Bagh Pact / Andhra Mahasabha

items.title: Potti Sreeramulu & the Formation of Andhra State (1952–53)
items.body:
## The fast that made a state

- **Potti Sreeramulu** began a **fast-unto-death** on **19 October 1952** demanding a separate Andhra State for the Telugu districts of Madras State.
- He **died on 15 December 1952**. His death set off violent agitation across the Telugu districts (seven killed in police firing).
- On **19 December 1952**, PM **Jawaharlal Nehru** announced the formation of a separate Andhra State. He is remembered as **Amarajeevi** (the immortal).

## Andhra State (1 October 1953)

- **Parliament passed the Andhra State Act in 1953**; on **1 October 1953**, **11 Telugu-speaking districts** of Madras State became **Andhra State**, with **Kurnool** as capital and the **High Court at Guntur**.
- It was **India's first state formed on a linguistic basis**.
- **Tanguturi Prakasam** ('Andhra Kesari') became the **first Chief Minister**; **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** was the last CM of Andhra State.
keyPoints: Potti Sreeramulu began his final fast on 19 October 1952 and died on 15 December 1952.
Nehru announced a separate Andhra State on 19 December 1952.
Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953 with Kurnool as capital — India's first linguistic state.
Andhra State comprised 11 Telugu districts of Madras State (Coastal Andhra + Rayalaseema).
Tanguturi Prakasam (Andhra Kesari) was the first CM; Bezawada Gopala Reddy the last.
items.mnemonic: '1-10-53, Kurnool': Andhra State born 1 Oct 1953 at Kurnool.

items.title: SRC, Gentlemen's Agreement & Birth of Andhra Pradesh (1956)
items.body:
## States Reorganisation Commission

- The **States Reorganisation Commission (SRC), 1953** — chaired by **Fazl Ali**, with **H. N. Kunzru** and **K. M. Panikkar** — submitted its report in **1955**, accepting **language** as a major basis for states.
- Its recommendations produced the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956** (in force 1 November 1956), backed by the **7th Constitutional Amendment**.

## Visalandhra and Telangana safeguards

- The **Visalandhra** movement sought to unite all Telugu speakers — Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema and **Telangana** (then in Hyderabad State).
- To reassure the less-developed Telangana, the **Gentlemen's Agreement (1956)** promised safeguards: a **Telangana Regional Committee**, protection of Telangana's **surplus revenues**, and **domicile rules** for jobs and education.

## Andhra Pradesh (1 November 1956)

- Andhra State merged with the **Telangana region** of Hyderabad State to form **Andhra Pradesh** on **1 November 1956**, with **Hyderabad** as capital.
- **Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy** became the **first Chief Minister** of Andhra Pradesh.
keyPoints: SRC (1953) was chaired by Fazl Ali with members H. N. Kunzru and K. M. Panikkar; report in 1955.
States Reorganisation Act, 1956 reorganised states on a linguistic basis (in force 1 Nov 1956).
Gentlemen's Agreement (1956) gave Telangana safeguards — Regional Committee, revenue, domicile rules.
Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956 by merging Andhra State with Telangana, capital Hyderabad.
Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy was the first CM of Andhra Pradesh.
items.mnemonic: 'FAKe' SRC = Fazl Ali, Kunzru, (Panikkar) — the linguistic-states commission.
items.source: Wikipedia — States Reorganisation Act, 1956; Andhra State; standard accounts of the Gentlemen's Agreement

items.title: Regional Agitations & the 2014 Bifurcation
items.body:
## Telangana movement (1969) and Jai Andhra (1972)

- Alleged breaches of the **Gentlemen's Agreement** and the **Mulki rules** (residence-based local preference for jobs/education) fed the **1969 Telangana agitation**, led by the **Telangana Praja Samithi** under **Marri Chenna Reddy**.
- When the **Supreme Court upheld the Mulki rules in 1972**, Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema launched the **Jai Andhra movement (1972)** demanding a separate Andhra state.
- The **Six-Point Formula (1973)** resolved both agitations; it was given effect through **Article 371-D** (32nd Amendment), providing equitable education and employment across regions.

## Bifurcation (2014)

- The Telangana demand revived strongly after 2000 under the **Telangana Rashtra Samithi (K. Chandrashekar Rao)**; the **Srikrishna Committee (2010)** examined it.
- The **Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014** (Lok Sabha 18 Feb, Rajya Sabha 20 Feb, assent 1 March 2014) fixed **2 June 2014** as the **appointed day**: **Telangana** became India's **29th state**.
- **Hyderabad** was made the **common capital for up to ten years**; **Amaravati** was planned as the capital of residuary Andhra Pradesh.
keyPoints: Mulki rules gave residence-based preference for local jobs/education; their breach fed the 1969 Telangana agitation.
1969 Telangana movement led by Telangana Praja Samithi under Marri Chenna Reddy.
Jai Andhra movement (1972) followed the Supreme Court upholding the Mulki rules.
Six-Point Formula (1973) was implemented via Article 371-D (32nd Amendment).
AP Reorganisation Act 2014: appointed day 2 June 2014; Telangana became the 29th state.
Hyderabad = common capital for up to 10 years; Amaravati = residuary AP capital.
items.mnemonic: '2-6-14, 29': Telangana born 2 June 2014 as the 29th state.
items.source: Wikipedia — Jai Andhra movement; Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014

items.title: District Reorganisation of AP (2014 → 2026)
items.body:
## Evolution of districts

| Date | Districts | Note |
|---|---|---|
| 2 Jun 2014 | 13 | Residuary AP at bifurcation |
| 4 Apr 2022 | 26 | Wholesale reorganisation |
| 31 Dec 2025 | **28** | +Polavaram, +Markapuram |

## The two newest districts (31 Dec 2025)

- **Polavaram** — HQ **Rampachodavaram**; carved from Alluri Sitharama Raju district; **least populous** district of AP.
- **Markapuram** — HQ Markapuram; carved from Prakasam district.

## Points to avoid confusing

- **Madanapalle is NOT a district** — it is the **headquarters of Annamayya district**. (A Nov-2025 '29 districts' proposal was not notified.)
- **28 zilla parishads** come into effect **25 September 2026**.
keyPoints: AP has 28 districts since 31 December 2025 (was 26 from 4 April 2022, 13 in 2014).
The two 2025 additions are Polavaram (HQ Rampachodavaram) and Markapuram (HQ Markapuram).
Polavaram is AP's least populous district; Madanapalle is the HQ of Annamayya district, not a district.
28 zilla parishads take effect from 25 September 2026.
items.source: Wikipedia (List of districts of Andhra Pradesh); AP-BRIEF ground truth — verified 29 Sep 2026
